clf-shared-responsibility-boundary.alt: EC2 and S3 responsibility comparison. Customers patch the EC2 guest OS, configure applications, set S3 bucket permissions, and choose encryption options. AWS runs the EC2 host and hypervisor, and the S3 service operating system and storage. Customers protect data and manage access in both services.

clf-access-decision-path.alt: An AWS principal makes a request with an action, resource, and conditions. AWS evaluates applicable policies before service access and an explicit deny overrides an allow.

clf-event-driven-service-flow.alt: An input S3 bucket sends an event to Lambda under an invoke permission. The function uses its separate execution role to read the input and write processed output to an independent bucket.

clf-cost-feedback-loop.alt: A pre-launch cost estimate, actual resource usage, AWS Cost Explorer analysis, AWS Budgets alerts, and the account owners' decision each have a separate role.

aif-ml-lifecycle.alt: Choose real-time, asynchronous, or batch inference by the time and form in which clients need results. A streaming response can return chunks during a real-time generation request.

aif-prompt-response.alt: The application sends a goal, approved context, and constraints to a foundation model. The response is checked against evidence. Tokens affect context size, latency, and cost.

aif-rag-flow.alt: Single prompting returns the model response, RAG supplies retrieved documents as evidence, and agents plan, get approval for some tools, act, and observe the result.

aif-model-evaluation.alt: Use representative and likely failure cases to assess model quality separately from business outcomes before making an acceptance decision.

aif-responsible-ai-controls.alt: Check representative data and subgroup performance, apply IAM authorization and input and output filters, and keep human review and production oversight.

aif-security-governance.alt: The AI application uses a scoped role for model calls and retrieval. Encryption, data controls, and audit logs apply at the relevant boundaries.

ans-global-ingress-round-trip.alt: DNS lookup and HTTPS request and response through CloudFront and a load balancer

ans-hybrid-multivpc-round-trip.alt: Hybrid request and reply through the same firewall endpoint in the inspection VPC

ans-vpc-routing-packet-walk.alt: A private subnet route table selects the VPC peer for 10.40.20.25 and the peer has a return route

ans-network-operations-evidence.alt: A comparison of Reachability Analyzer, which evaluates network configuration without sending packets, and VPC Flow Logs, which record observed IP traffic. Compare both kinds of evidence, change one relevant setting, and retest the same connection.

ans-network-security-layered-controls.alt: Inbound HTTPS and S3 access in a workload VPC, with separate records for configuration changes

saa-secure-vpc-path.alt: Multi-AZ VPC placement of internet-facing ALB nodes, private application targets, and Amazon RDS. Example connections show which network and access-control boundaries each leg crosses.

saa-rds-recovery-boundaries.alt: Three RDS recovery examples compare the standby in another Availability Zone, a backup and logs copied to a second Region, and point-in-time recovery to a new database following a deletion.

saa-performance-path.alt: A CloudFront cache hit returns to the browser at the edge. A cache miss reaches an internet-facing ALB and a private application target. Measurement points separate user response time from origin and target time.

dva-event-processing-contract.alt: Synchronous order acceptance and asynchronous SQS worker processing with retry and dead-letter isolation

dva-request-identity-and-secret-flow.alt: Application role credentials, limited secret access, and time-limited signed URL boundaries

dva-pipeline-release-gates.alt: Release pipeline with quality and monitoring gates, canary deployment, and rollback

dva-observability-feedback-loop.alt: Observability evidence loop from correlated signals through triage and safe remediation

soa-observability-remediation-loop.alt: Orders API traffic and its dependency, the distinct signals in CloudWatch, CloudWatch Logs, and CloudTrail, and approved Systems Manager Automation followed by a check of the same metrics.

soa-progressive-change-control.alt: A load balancer directs production requests to stable and canary targets. A separate release control area shows infrastructure change review, scoped rollout, and the metric-based decision to expand or restore a known-good state.

soa-network-request-return-path.alt: DNS resolves the public ALB separately from HTTPS. Within the VPC, the ALB node in a public subnet opens a second connection to a target in a private subnet. Check routes, security groups and subnet ACLs for each leg.

scs-evidence-trail-boundaries.alt: A CloudTrail trail delivers management events and selected S3 GetObject and PutObject data events to a restricted encrypted log archive. GuardDuty produces a finding from configured sources, and an analyst returns to the applicable original record during triage.

scs-edge-origin-boundary.alt: A browser reaches CloudFront as the only public viewer entry. CloudFront uses a VPC origin with an internal Application Load Balancer and private application targets. AWS WAF evaluates requests at its CloudFront or ALB association; the internal ALB has no public direct-origin path.

scs-cross-account-assume-role-boundary.alt: A partner workload uses AWS STS AssumeRole with an ExternalId to obtain temporary credentials for an IAM role in the customer account. Trust policy controls entry, while the role permission policy restricts use to an approved S3 bucket prefix; a bucket policy can add further conditions.

dea-data-ingestion-flow.alt: Compare batch files and streaming events, then follow immutable raw input through validation, quarantine, transformation, and publication.

dea-data-ownership-and-catalog.alt: The dataset owner defines quality, classification, retention and terms. The platform stores the data and catalog separately, and consumers direct issues to the steward.

dea-stream-replay-and-recovery.alt: A checkpoint records normal processing progress. An operator can select a replay range from retained input and use an idempotent output update.

dea-data-access-permissions.alt: Analyst and ETL roles receive distinct authorization scopes. The catalog describes the data, which is stored in S3, encrypted with KMS and monitored by audit records.

sap-hybrid-network-boundaries.alt: The on-premises network and AWS VPC meet at a hybrid routing boundary. Compare the normal Direct Connect path and the independent VPN route.

sap-migration-wave-and-cutover.alt: Group workloads by dependency before moving a wave. Validate replicated data and service health before cutover, and retain a rollback path while it is safe.

sap-safe-change-and-remediation.alt: A deployment changes a limited scope. Signals can trigger a guarded recovery action, which is verified before the change proceeds or wider remediation occurs.

feature-time-boundary.alt: Only data available at the prediction time can be used as features. A later confirmed outcome can be used as a training label.

threshold-decision-cost.alt: The alert threshold trades missed positives against false alarms. Set it using the cost of each mistake and the capacity to investigate alerts.

ground-truth-monitoring-boundaries.alt: Monitor changes in inputs and predictions independently of model quality. Measure quality by comparing predictions with ground truth when outcomes arrive later.

mla-inference-decision-timing.alt: Compare an application that receives each prediction from a SageMaker endpoint with a batch job that reads an S3 dataset and saves predictions in S3 for later review.

mla-data-lineage.alt: Trace the source, transformation, training data and model artifact. Preserve the versions, execution identity and evaluation data at handoffs.

mla-inference-mode-boundaries.alt: Compare a real-time endpoint with immediate responses, asynchronous requests queued for an endpoint with output in S3, and a Batch Transform job over a bounded dataset.

mla-progressive-deployment.alt: Promote the evaluated model to limited traffic and check quality, latency, errors, cost and safety. Expand only after the gate passes, with a known good model for rollback.
